# Data clean-up

Ok great got the terminal set up and now we just need to get this good stuff into R and do some data transformations
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

setwd ("/Users/alex/UO_codes/comptools/hw2_alex")
out_dir <- "./data"
raw_data <- read_tsv("./data/Stickle_RNAseq.tsv")
range <- 5:ncol(raw_data)
long_fish <- pivot_longer(raw_data, 
    cols = range, 
    names_to = "Gene",
    values_to = "Expression") #defines the value or measurement
write.csv(long_fish, file.path(out_dir, "long_fish.csv"))
```

Long formatted data is looking good, but how am I to choose which genes to look at without making a table to give me a statistical summary of all of them so I can choose which are the most interesting?

# Finding most variable genes

Here is the code for the second plot

```{r}
summary_table <- long_fish |>
    group_by(Gene) |>
     summarise(n = n(),
            mean = mean(Expression),
            sd = sd(Expression),
            median = median(Expression),)
    write.csv(summary_table, file.path(out_dir, "gene_expression_summary.csv"),  row.names = FALSE)
```

Now I want to look at the most highly variable genes, gonna steal this straight from the single cell book. Except I will not be rewritting everything into a Seurat object and instead just doing it the good old fasion way

## Log transformation
```{r}
log_fish <- summary_table |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), log))
write.csv(log_fish, file.path(out_dir, "log_gene_expression_summary.csv"),  row.names = FALSE)
```

asked claude how to use `mutate` to get log of only numberic values

Now plotting mean and variance onto the same grah
```{r}
plot_dir <- "./results"

HVG_plot <- ggplot(log_fish, aes(x = mean, y = sd)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, color = "#4A5759") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#EDAF88") +
  labs(title = "Stickleback Highly Variable Genes", subtitle = "expression counts are log-transformed", x = "Mean expression", y = "expression varience")
ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "Stickle_HVG.png"), plot = HVG_plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

ok great so I have my plot, but I want to determine, which genes are actually the most variable. To do this I started by asking claude how I could get the vector value of each point from the line of best fit.

## Fidning top HVG

```{r}
resid_df <- log_fish |>
  mutate(fit_sd  = predict(lm(sd ~ mean)),
         dist    = sd - fit_sd,
         dist_z  = dist / stats::sd(dist),
         high    = dist_z > 1.5) |>
  ungroup() 
write.csv(resid_df, file.path(out_dir, "resid_df.csv"),  row.names = FALSE)
  
```

Asked Claude how I can get the distance of each point from the line of best fit or expected vector. Fitted is the y value the regression line prediects, and then we subract the actual y from that to see if it is above or below. Then it gets transformed into units of redisual sd. I moved the standard cutoff or high to be 1.5 because there is not a ton of varience, which yeilded 12 highly variable genes.

Now let's plot the genes that were the farthest from the line
```{r}
library(ggrepel)


HVG_plot <- ggplot(resid_df, aes(x = mean, y = sd)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = dist_z > 1.5), size = 2,) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#EDAF88") +
  geom_text_repel(data = filter(resid_df, dist_z > 1.5),
                  aes(label = Gene)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#B0C4B1", "TRUE" = "#4A5759"),
                     guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Stickleback Highly Variable Genes", subtitle = "expression counts are log-transformed", x = "Mean expression", y = "expression variance")
ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "Labeled_Stickle_HVG.png"), plot = HVG_plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

with much trial and error between me and Claude I was able to label and color the specific genes of interest based on their `dist_z` which acts as explaining how much of the varience can be explained by relationship to mean, and which genes have greater-than-expected varient values

making violin plot

```{r}
four_fish_violin <- log_long_fish |>
  filter(Gene %in% c("Gene280", "Gene361", "Gene448", "Gene526")) |>
  ggplot(aes(Genotype, Expression, fill = Microbiota)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.4, color = NA, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Microbiota), alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2,
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.08, dodge.width = 0.8)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(end = 0.7) + scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ Gene, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Host genotype", y = "Read count of each gene",
       title = "Stickleback gut RNA-seq of four most variable genes",
       subtitle = "Each point is one fish; violins show the full distribution") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(legend.position = "top")
 ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "My_gene_violin.png"), plot = four_fish_violin, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```
